title: PRD: Hosted API runtime decision log, acceptance matrix, and launch sanity
creator: Ava Collins
description: This PRD captures product requirements, runtime-level decisions, and an operational acceptance matrix for launching the consolidated Hosted API surface (chat, completions, embeddings, rerank). It documents behavioral contracts, performance budgets, degraded-mode fallbacks, compatibility constraints, and a runbook for canary -> staged rollout. Purpose: reduce ambiguity between PM/Eng/Design, lock measurable acceptance criteria, and record trade-offs that affect launch scope.
scope: Include: chat/completions/embeddings/rerank endpoints for hosted customers with streaming and non-streaming flows, function/tool-calling surface for chat, structured JSON output guarantees for selected schemas, model pinning per-customer, and regional routing policies. Exclude: multimodal file uploads, experimental quantized model variants in private deployments, and dedicated capacity autoscaler UX (handled in separate project).
scope_changes: Initial draft allowed experimental kernel-level optimizations in hosted. After perf validation (ENG-34121) we scoped that to post-launch: the launch will rely on validated kernel selection only; aggressive kernel switching is postponed. Also deferred: embedding top-k caching eviction tuning for launch window (ship with default eviction heuristics, iterate post-launch).
decisions: Runtime will expose per-route 'latency profile' setting: low-latency, balanced, high-throughput. Default: balanced for free-tier, low-latency for enterprise lanes.
Fallback chain: preferred model variant -> compatible quantized variant -> cross-region fallback -> rate-limited simple heuristic responder (for critical SLA lanes only).
Streaming API semantics will preserve token order and include a final metadata envelope with deterministic fields (request_id, model_version, token_count, truncated boolean).
Compatibility: The new endpoint is backward-compatible with existing gen/streaming semantics; deprecation warnings will be emitted for legacy query params for 90 days post-launch.
Telemetry: All requests must include trace_id and receive latency attribution to model, network, and batching windows.
tradeoffs: Performance vs determinism: enabling continuous aggressive batching reduces cost but increases tail latency variance. We chose conservative batching by default to meet latency SLOs and expose a toggle for throughput-optimized lanes. Cost vs fidelity: early quantized model variants yield cost savings but showed rare coherence regressions in regression harness; quantized variants will be 'opt-in' for customers and not the default at launch.
acceptance_criteria: Functional: chat/completions/embeddings/rerank endpoints accept documented request schema and return documented response schema for 99.9% of integration tests in the conformance harness.
Latency: p95 end-to-end latency (customer-observed) <= 300ms for small chat requests (<=128 tokens) on low-latency lane and <= 600ms on balanced lane across US regions.
Throughput: Dedicated staging pool sustains 500 concurrent balanced-lane requests with <2% 5xx error rate during sustained load run (30m).
Quality: embeddings cosine similarity regression vs baseline model within +/-0.02 on benchmark dataset; rerank NDCG drop <= 0.01 vs baseline for canonical queries.
Stability: rollback path verified: automated fallback to previous model variant completes within 90s under simulated degraded kernel (test harness ENG-34444).
Observability: request-level telemetry (trace_id, model_version, route, latency breakdown) visible in Console for last 7 days and surfaced in canary dashboard prior to traffic ramp.
Operational: canary plan executed with 0 customer-facing errors for 24h at 1% traffic, and gradual ramp steps documented in runbook.
Security/Compliance: KMS key access verified for customer-supplied keys in private deployments; SAML/OIDC sign-on flows for console validated with security review.
